examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Acceleration of a Particle
examples.problem: A particle moves with constant acceleration. When $t=0 \, \textrm{h},$ the velocity of the particle is $4\mathbf{i}  \, \textrm{km/h},$ and when $t=3\, \textrm{h},$ the velocity of the particle is $(7\mathbf{i}+15\mathbf{j})  \, \textrm{km/h}.$ Calculate the acceleration of the particle.
examples.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
\mathbf{v} = \mathbf{u} + \mathbf{a}t,
$$

where $\mathbf{u}$ is the initial velocity, and $\mathbf{a}$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Substituting 

$$
\mathbf{u} = 4\mathbf{i}, \qquad
\mathbf{v} = 7\mathbf{i}+15\mathbf{j}, \qquad
t =3
$$

into the equation above, we can solve for $\mathbf{a}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\ 7i+15j & =4i+a(3) \\ 3i+15j & =3a \\ a & =\frac{1}{3}(3i+15j) \\ a & =(i+5j)\,{\text{km/h}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: The initial velocity of a particle is $(5i-j)\,\text{km/h}.$ Find the speed of the particle after $2$ hours if the particle moves with a constant acceleration of $(i+3j)\,{\text{km/h}}^{2}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Here, we have

$$
u=5i-j,\,a=i+3j.
$$

Therefore, after $2$ hours, the velocity of the particle will be

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\  & =(5i-j)+(i+3j)(2) \\  & =(5i-j)+(2i+6j) \\  & =(7i+5j)\,\text{km/h}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the speed of the particle is

$$
\begin{aligned}|v| & =|7i+5j| \\  & =\sqrt{{7}^{2}+{5}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{49+25} \\  & =\sqrt{74}\,\text{km/h}.\end{aligned}
$$
